summary: This note covers the 1952 recording history of the song "You Belong to Me". Joni James made the first 1952 recording in Chicago after seeing the sheet music in the Woods Building, and it was released on the local Sharp Records label and later reissued on M-G-M. Sue Thompson and Patti Page then recorded versions on Mercury, and Patti Page's version entered the Billboard chart on August 22, 1952, peaking at No. 4. The note appears twice in the source with slightly different wording about the MGM reissue; the facts below reflect the shared content.
one_line: Chronicles the 1952 recordings of the song "You Belong to Me" by Joni James, Sue Thompson and Patti Page and its Billboard chart run.
key_facts: Joni James made the first 1952 recording of the song.
Joni James had seen the sheet music in the Woods Building in Chicago and the lyrics attracted her.
Joni James recorded the song in February 1952 in Chicago.
Joni James's recording was released in March 1952 on the local Sharp Records label.
Joni James's version was reissued as her second single on August 5, 1952, after she signed to MGM.
Joni James's version was also issued on M-G-M Records for national distribution.
Jo Stafford, Patti Page and Dean Martin had covered the song before August 5, 1952.
The best-known early 1952 version was recorded by Sue Thompson on Mercury's country label as catalog number 6407.
Patti Page's version was issued by Mercury as catalog number 5899.
Patti Page's version had "I Went to Your Wedding" on the flip side.
"I Went to Your Wedding" was a bigger Patti Page hit, reaching No. 1.
Patti Page's version entered the Billboard chart on August 22, 1952.
Patti Page's version lasted 12 weeks on the Billboard chart.
Patti Page's version peaked at No. 4 on the Billboard chart.
